# Compliance and Change-Control Policy Enforcement Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that policy evaluation, exceptions, blocking, and change control are defined and non-bypassable
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Legend**: `[M]` mandatory (a constitution MUST, an approved requirement, or an approved decision); `[O]` optional enhancement or backlog boundary. `G0` is evaluable now against the approved specification, plan, ADRs, and contracts; `G1` is evaluable after `/speckit-tasks` and `/speckit-analyze`, before implementation. `{Detects: ...}` links an item to a failure pattern in the [README](README.md) detection matrix. Dimension tags: Completeness, Clarity, Consistency, Measurability, Coverage, Traceability, Edge Case, Assumption, Conflict, Gap.
## Policy Model and Versioning

- [ ] CHK001 - Is a versioned catalogue defined covering security, compliance, privacy, audit retention, approved dependencies, licensing, and change control? [Completeness, Spec FR-124, Constitution VI] [M, G0] {Detects: missing-policy-evaluation}
- [ ] CHK002 - Is every constitution MUST cited by a mandatory policy, with a completeness check in both directions? [Traceability, Spec DEC-048, ADR-014] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is a recorded policy version required on every run, with a run lacking one defined as a failure? [Coverage, Spec FR-101, POL-CHG-001] [M, G0] {Detects: policy-without-version}
- [ ] CHK004 - Must every applicable check produce exactly one of the four outcomes per evaluation point, with no outcome defined as a failure? [Measurability, Spec FR-124 NAC] [M, G0] {Detects: missing-policy-evaluation}
- [ ] CHK005 - Are evaluation points defined for each stage (after normalize, design, before implement, after test, compliance check, release readiness, change, replan)? [Completeness, Compliance §2.5] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK006 - Are mandatory, advisory, and non-waivable policies defined consistently between the catalogue and the specification? [Consistency, ADR-014, Spec DEC-064] [M, G0]

## Blocking and Exceptions

- [ ] CHK007 - Is a failed mandatory policy defined as blocking all downstream progression, with the block window and its safe-stop? [Clarity, Spec FR-125, DEC-045] [M, G0] {Detects: compliance-failure-not-blocking}
- [ ] CHK008 - Is a downstream node starting while a mandatory FAIL is unresolved defined as a detectable violation? [Measurability, Spec FR-125 NAC] [M, G0] {Detects: compliance-failure-not-blocking}
- [ ] CHK009 - Does the exception workflow require all fields (policy, reason, scope, approving authority, compensating control, timestamp, expiry or review condition) and reject incomplete exceptions? [Completeness, Spec FR-125, Constitution VI] [M, G0] {Detects: missing-compensating-control}
- [ ] CHK010 - Is an exception lacking human approval (agent-approved or inferred) defined as invalid and ineffective? [Coverage, Spec FR-125 NAC] [M, G0] {Detects: unapproved-exception}
- [ ] CHK011 - Is exception expiry or review defined with its effect (returns to BLOCKING) and the time it is checked? [Clarity, Spec FR-128 NAC, ADR-014] [M, G0] {Detects: expired-exception}
- [ ] CHK012 - Is CONDITIONAL_PASS defined as a derived disposition (FAIL retained, compensating control documented, human-accepted at G-RISK and G-REL, never for non-waivable policies)? [Clarity, ADR-014, Spec DEC-096, DEC-108] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is the readiness definition in the specification (FR-128, ASM-013) reconciled with ADR-014, or tracked through change control? [Conflict, Spec FR-128, ADR-014] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is release readiness deterministic with every blocking item listed, including conditions? [Measurability, Spec FR-128, Readiness contract] [M, G0]

## Change Control

- [ ] CHK015 - Is formal impact analysis plus change approval required before any change to approved requirements, architecture, schemas, workflow states, security controls, or release criteria takes effect? [Coverage, Spec FR-126, Constitution VI] [M, G0] {Detects: material-change-without-impact-analysis}
- [ ] CHK016 - Is that approval requirement defined for architecture, schema, security, and workflow-state changes, with an unapproved change defined as a violation? [Coverage, Spec FR-126 NAC, POL-CHG-005] [M, G0] {Detects: change-without-formal-approval}
- [ ] CHK017 - Is "material change" defined by artifact kind and used consistently in replanning, approvals, and change control? [Clarity, Spec DEC-046] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK018 - Is the change record defined (owner, version impact, compatibility, consumers, tests, docs, rollout, approval), with a failure when declared and computed impact differ? [Completeness, Change-record schema] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK019 - Is a revalidation matrix defined for downstream artifacts per upstream change? [Completeness, Compliance §8] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are policy outcomes, exceptions, and the catalogue version required in audit and traceability evidence? [Coverage, POL-CHG-007] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK021 - Are the blocking demonstrations RB-1..5 defined with expected outputs, including negative cases? [Measurability, Compliance §4.2] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is a formal fifth policy outcome (constitution amendment) labelled an optional alternative? [Boundary, ADR-014 option C] [O, G0]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Gap]` or `[Conflict]` name a place where the current documents are silent or disagree; they are findings for the reviewer to resolve, not pre-judged results
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially within this file (`CHK001` onward); cite them as `<file>:CHKnnn`
